subject: Capacity onramp: staggered min-commit offer and warm-start lanes for PhoenixAI
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Zhao <elaine.zhao@phoenixai.com>
Cc: procurement@phoenixai.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity onramp: staggered min-commit offer and warm-start lanes for PhoenixAI

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the time today. Based on what you shared about production traffic patterns (90% conversational inference, bursty daytime peaks in US-East, and model mix with two heavy variants), I've put together a lightweight proposal that gives PhoenixAI predictable baseline capacity with a controlled ramp and warm-start credits to reduce cold-start latency during the first 60 days.

Attached: PXI_capacity_proposal_20261003.pdf and an editable workbook (PXI_onramp_workbook_20261003.xlsx) that has the inputs we used. Highlights: 
- Initial min-commit: 24 GPUs (reserved) for a 30-day stabilization window
- Week 5–12 staged ramp to 64 GPUs (reserve) in two tranches (adds 20 GPUs at week 5, +20 at week 9)
- Warm-start buffer: 10% of fleet kept in warm pools for prefix caching (reduces tail latency)
- Burst allowance: 30% burst via preemptible lanes (best-effort) and paid burst credits
- Canary & fallback: dedicated canary lane + automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant if latency SLOs degrade

Cost and credits are summarized in the first tab of the PDF. The workbook contains alternative ramp curves (aggressive / conservative) — feel free to edit and send back.

Next step: if this looks reasonable, can your procurement lead (cc'd) confirm timeline constraints and any PO cadence? We're happy to convert this into a formal quote and provide a 30-day trial of the warm-start buffer at no additional charge to validate latency.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Rep, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Capacity onramp: staggered min-commit offer and warm-start lanes for PhoenixAI

Jonas —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the workbook. High level this matches what our infra team expects. A couple of clarification items before we loop procurement formally: 
1) Can you confirm the SLA targets tied to the reserved baseline vs. burst lanes?
2) For the warm-start buffer, is that implemented as persistent prefix caches on reserved instances, or as a managed cache layer? How is cache invalidation handled with model updates?
3) We need a clear decommit path if our usage doesn't materialize after month 3. Is there an early-stepdown mechanism?

Michael (cc) will own procurement logistics. We'll aim to review and get you feedback by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Elaine
Head of Infrastructure, PhoenixAI
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-04T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: FW: PXI clarifications — SLA, warm-start details, decommit path

Looping you in to confirm technical/contract answers so we can respond to Elaine today. Specific asks:
- SLA: need wording for reserved baseline (p99 < 220ms token) and best-effort burst lanes (no SLA, advisory). Also note fallback variant guarantee (quantized model) with p99 < 350ms.
- Warm-start: Karthik, please provide the implementation summary and monitoring hooks we can include.
- Decommit: Ben/Marissa — pricing/legal: can we offer a stepdown after 90 days with a 30-day notice that reduces committed GPUs by up to 40% without penalty? Need exact language and any minimum floor.

Also advise if we should propose a small onboarding credit or pilot pricing for month 1 to accelerate sign-off.

Thanks,
Jonas
On 2026-10-04 10:52:00-07:00, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PXI clarifications — SLA, warm-start details, decommit path

Jonas — quick technical write-up for Elaine (paste into reply):

SLA / Performance guarantees- Reserved baseline (committed GPUs): we guarantee network and GPU availability for scheduled capacity. For the baseline fleet we propose a production SLO of p95 < 160ms per token and p99 < 220ms for the model family you described, measured end-to-end from request to first token.
- Burst lanes: preemptible / spot lanes are explicitly best-effort and excluded from SLAs; they are meant for throughput spikes and batch backfills.
- Fallback model: when latency or hardware contention triggers, routing policy will fall back to the compatible quantized variant (same weights, 8-bit quantized) — expected p99 < 350ms.

Warm-start buffer implementation- Warm-start = managed prefix/KV warm pools pinned to reserved hosts (logical warm slots). We'll keep ~10% of reserved GPUs in warm state for the first 60 days and tune based on cold-start observed percentiles in week 1.
- Cache invalidation: we support model rollout hooks; when you push a model update we run an invalidation job that sequences warm caches (evict then preprime) with a rolling window to avoid a cold-surge. We can expose metrics (cache_hit_ratio, cold_start_rate) in the Console and add tracing hooks to the canary route.

Decommit / stepdown policy- We can offer a ‘90-day stabilization’ clause: after day 90 PhoenixAI may request one stepdown event that reduces committed GPUs by up to 40% with a 30-day notice. Each subsequent stepdown requires 60 days notice and is limited to 20% of remaining committed capacity. Min floor: 12 GPUs retained as the minimum committed baseline for the contract to remain active.

Additional ops notes- Canary: we recommend a 2-GPU dedicated canary lane with custom tracing for any release.
- Autoscale guardrails: maintain continuous batching at 8–16 concurrent requests per GPU; we’ll tune batch thresholds based on the workbook traffic mix.

I can produce a one-page technical appendix to attach to the proposal if you want.

—Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PXI clarifications — SLA, warm-start details, decommit path

Thanks — approve adding the technical appendix and the 90-day stabilization clause. Contract/legal endorsed the stepdown language but insisted on a hard minimum floor of 12 GPUs and a single-stepdown event in the first 120 days. For commercial: we can offer the warm-start buffer free for the first 30 days and a 7% onboarding credit applied to month 1 invoice to help offset migration testing.

Jonas: update the PDF with the SLA bullets, the technical appendix (Karthik), and the revised stepdown language and send to Elaine/procurement. Marissa — can you approve a 7% onboarding credit for this deal? If approved I’ll finalize the quote.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
